question.problem:
Consider the following parametric equation of the parabola 

$$
x-1=3t,\,y+4={t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of this parabola is

$(x\,-$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x-1}{3},\,{t}^{2}=y+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(\frac{x-1}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=y+4$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9} & =y+4 \\ {(x-1)}^{2} & =9(y+4)\end{aligned}
$$
